labels.label: lem:precausalite_engendre_minimale
labels.notes: Unmarked, REPORT status partial: correct. Causal.Precausality.generated_absolutelyMinimalOn_all has hypotheses hU (cover) and hA : ∀ i, ∀ W ≤ U i, (P i).AbsolutelyMinimalOn W, and concludes ∀ W, (generated U hU P).AbsolutelyMinimalOn W. No compatibility and no Baire hypothesis. This is the paper's lemma (ETT.tex:498-501) in the hereditary reading: hereditary pieces give a hereditary result. The M-only reading is the library's marked anchor Precausality.generated_absolutelyMinimal (hypothesis AbsolutelyMinimalOn (U i), conclusion AbsolutelyMinimal); its signature was checked. Causal.generated_single_transparentLine (one chart U = ⊤ carrying transparentLine) proves that the library's hypothesis AbsolutelyMinimalOn (U i) does not give the hereditary conclusion. The statement is right and not vacuous. The reading 'absolutely minimal on U_i' = 'on every open subset of U_i' is raised and left undecided, in the REPORT question (OQ-95) and in Generated.lean SCOPE ('Which reading is the formalization of record is the author's'). One wording slip, at Generated.lean:45 (minor finding 3).

labels.label: ex:open_subset
labels.notes: Unmarked, REPORT status partial: correct. The library's ex:open_subset module (Causal/Morphism.lean) also leaves it unmarked. Finding 1 was checked against ETT.tex:258-263 and the library's definitions. LocalCausality.InclusionStrong L C is ∀ U, (L.le (U ⊓ W) → C.le U) ∧ (L.lt (U ⊓ W) → C.lt U), and LocalCausality.inclusionStrong_iff proves it equivalent to StrongMorphism L.toSubtype C Subtype.val, the DEC-10/DEC-12 strong morphism: an open continuous map whose components φ⁻¹U → U preserve ≤ and ≪, with no reflection. Causal.openSubset_not_unique_of_absolutelyMinimal exhibits L₁ = timelikeLine.restrict ⊤ and L₂ = LocalCausality.diagonal ⊤. Both are InclusionStrong for timelikeLine, both have toSubtype absolutely minimal on every open of ↥⊤ (hereditary, so also M-only by absolutelyMinimal_iff), and they differ (L₁.le ⊤ 0 1, ¬ L₂.le ⊤ 0 1). The open set W = ℝ, with its subspace topology, is second countable and Hausdorff. So the Lean statement is exactly the negation of the printed first-sentence uniqueness, under the ruled strong morphism, with the gluing field in either form. It is the paper's claim, not a different one. Does it contradict DEC-167? Yes for the first sentence: 'uniqueness in ex:open_subset holds as printed' is false for l.260 under DEC-10/12, whichever form the field takes, because gluing does not touch the diagonal (it is glued on every open). No for the second sentence (l.262): under either form every causality is absolutely minimal, so LocalIsomorphism.unique (Morphism.lean:689; its signature takes C₁.AbsolutelyMinimal and C₂.AbsolutelyMinimal) gives uniqueness as printed. No for prop:GX_espace_temps_topo (see that row). The diagonal witness was already in the text of OQ-13, which DEC-167 rules. The author therefore has to choose among: (i) DEC-167's clause covers the second sentence only; (ii) a strong morphism of an inclusion is read as reflecting the relations (then InclusionStrong.eq_restrict gives uniqueness, and existence needs the hereditary field); (iii) 'greatest' (InclusionStrong.le_restrict). This is an OQ for the author, not the closer's to settle (minor finding 2). Existence findings (2), checked: Causal.transparentLine_restrict_toSubtype_not_absolutelyMinimal (transparentLine.AbsolutelyMinimal ∧ ¬ (transparentLine.restrict realMinusZero).toSubtype.AbsolutelyMinimal) and Causal.transparentLine_pullback_val_not_absolutelyMinimal (the same along ↥realMinusZero → ℝ). Both say exactly what the REPORT says. The REPORT correctly adds that l.260 existence survives under the M-only field through the diagonal, and it leaves l.262 existence under the M-only field as an open question. Its argued example, the timelike line on ℝ ∖ {0} as a local isomorphism to the transparent line, is right: on small intervals away from 0 the two relations coincide. Under the hereditary field restrict_toSubtype_absolutelyMinimalOn_all and pullback_absolutelyMinimalOn_all_of_isLocalHomeomorph give existence. With pullback_localIsomorphism and LocalIsomorphism.unique, the second sentence therefore holds as printed under the hereditary field.

labels.label: prop:GX_espace_temps_topo
labels.notes: Unmarked, REPORT status partial; the anchor and its readings (DEC-12, DEC-16) are the library's. Causal.existsUnique_causality_GX_absolutelyMinimalOn_all keeps exactly the hypotheses of the library's existsUnique_causality_GX_maximal: D causally arc-connected, and G acting by StrongMorphism D D. Its conclusion is ∃ C, (every chart of the maximal atlas is a ChartIso) ∧ (∀ W, C.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W) ∧ (∀ C', charts iso → C'.AbsolutelyMinimal → C' = C). Uniqueness is among M-only absolutely minimal causalities, so it holds under either form of the field, as DEC-167 says. Existence is hereditary. Causal.existsUnique_absolutelyMinimalOn_all_of_agree_locally strengthens the library's existsUnique_absolutelyMinimal_of_agree_locally in the same way (same hypotheses, hereditary conclusion). X Baire and M second countable Hausdorff are not used ('weakened', disclosed).

Here sierpinskiCausality (le U x y := (x = y ∧ x ∈ U) ∨ U = ⊤) is hereditary by Precausality.absolutelyMinimalOn_prop, sierpinskiMap : Bool → Prop is continuous and not open, and the pullback relates false to true in ⊤ while the cover by singletons only has trivial steps. Two gluings (Gluing.causality = Causality.generated over Bool pieces; FamilyGlueData.causality): hereditary inputs give hereditary output, with no CompatibleAlong. ofOpensCausality is definitionally a pullback along the inclusion (#print). findings.what: Finding 1 is correct and should reach the author. Two things go with it. (a) It holds under the DEC-10/DEC-12 strong morphism, where components preserve the relations without reflecting them. The finding says 'a strong morphism only asks the relations of W to imply those of M' but does not cite the ruling, and gluing is beside the point here: under a reflecting reading the printed uniqueness is true even without gluing (InclusionStrong.eq_restrict). (b) The last sentence says the existing corrected forms ('greatest'; unique when reflecting) 'remain the true ones', with no qualification. Under the M-only field the restriction they characterise is in general not itself a causality of W (transparentLine_restrict_toSubtype_not_absolutelyMinimal), so as existence statements they hold only under the hereditary field. Separately, notes (4) says 'DEC-167's sentence on ex:open_subset should be read as the second sentence only'. That is an interpretation of an author ruling; the loop does not rule.
findings.fix: When forwarding: say 'under DEC-10/DEC-12's strong morphism'; qualify 'remain the true ones' with 'as existence statements, under the hereditary field'; and have the master open an OQ row (DEC-167 vs the diagonal witness, options (i)-(iii) in the ex:open_subset label notes of this audit) instead of adopting the closer's reading of DEC-167.

findings.what: The checklist parenthetical '(the paper's proof uses it on `W ∩ U_i` only, which is an open subset of `U_i`)' misdescribes ETT.tex:508. The paper invokes absolute minimality on U (its own gloss: 'quantified over every open cover of U and every open subset of U'), with the cover (O_a ∩ U)_a of U, applied to the open subset W ∩ U. That is the library's M-only AbsolutelyMinimalOn (U i). The hereditary lemma instead needs AbsolutelyMinimalOn (W ⊓ U i), for covers of W ⊓ U i only (Generated.lean:85), because the conclusion's covers cover only W. That is the reading's strengthening, not what the paper's proof uses. The marker '⚠ in the hereditary reading' is also outside kb/0006's vocabulary (✓ carried / ⚠ weakened / ⚠ strengthened). The SCOPE and the REPORT question state the reading correctly, so this is wording only.
findings.fix: Rewrite the row as '⚠ strengthened (reading, OQ-95): absolutely minimal on every open subset of U i; the paper's proof uses absolute minimality on U_i, which gives only the M-only conclusion (library generated_absolutelyMinimal; generated_single_transparentLine)'.

the_three_findings_for_the_author.1_ex_open_subset_uniqueness: TRUE, under the ruled reading of strong morphism (DEC-10/DEC-12). The Lean statement is the negation of ETT.tex:260's uniqueness with the gluing field in either form. It contradicts DEC-167's 'uniqueness in ex:open_subset holds as printed' for the first sentence only. The second sentence (LocalIsomorphism.unique, among absolutely minimal causalities, which under gluing is all of them) and prop:GX_espace_temps_topo (existsUnique_causality_GX_absolutelyMinimalOn_all) agree with DEC-167. The contradiction comes from the direction of the morphism, not from gluing: the diagonal causality is glued on every open set.
the_three_findings_for_the_author.2_existence_under_M_only_field: TRUE as stated. Under the M-only field the library's witnesses for l.260 ((C.restrict W).toSubtype) and for l.262 (the pullback, even along the open embedding ℝ ∖ {0} → ℝ) are not absolutely minimal for the transparent-point line. l.260 existence still holds through the diagonal. l.262 existence under the M-only field is open in general (the REPORT question), though it holds in the transparent-line example through the timelike line on ℝ ∖ {0} (argued; the argument is correct). Under the hereditary field both witnesses are glued.
the_three_findings_for_the_author.3_puncturedPlane: TRUE. Causal.puncturedPlane (Causal/LinesReachable.lean:584) is Causality.ofRelation R S on the T₂.₅ subspace ℝ² ∖ {0}, and S relates (1,1) to (2,2), off the diagonal. So by ofRelation_absolutelyMinimal_iff it is not absolutely minimal, and under DEC-167 it is not a causality. It is the witness of Causal.hypothesis_a_needed (LinesReachable.lean:750, rem:K_plongement_hypotheses, ETT.tex:951). The planner's non-minimal list omits it, so T-abs-gluing-retype must restate that remark's '(a) cannot be dispensed with' with a glued witness. This finding is about the library's witness, not about the paper's text. The sibling proves the same fact (Causal/GluingModels/NonMinimal.lean:166, puncturedPlane_not_minimal), a duplicate to merge.

notes: Optional, not a defect: the non-open pullback counterexample uses a non-Hausdorff target (disclosed in Pullback.lean SCOPE). A Hausdorff witness also exists, though its source is not second countable: φ = id : (ℝ, discrete) → ℝ pulls the timelike line back to a precausality relating 0 to 1 on ⊤, while the cover by singletons has only trivial steps (PullLink needs φ '' W₀ open). It is not formalized here. The REPORT's duplicates_to_merge list with the sibling was checked: the names differ and do not clash.
